title: Detecting isomorphisms on the pro-etale site
statement:
Let $\Lambda$ be a finite discrete ring and $T$ a scheme. Use left module sheaves and the derived categories of [def-weil-pbc-proetale-modules]. An isomorphism of complexes below means an isomorphism in the derived category, not a degreewise isomorphism of the chosen complexes.

1. **Locality for covering families.** A morphism $u:F\to G$ in $D(T_{\mathrm{proet}},\Lambda)$ is an isomorphism if and only if its inverse image along every member of one pro-etale covering family $\{U_i\to T\}$ [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site] is an isomorphism. A complex is acyclic if and only if every cohomology sheaf vanishes; a sheaf vanishes if and only if its restrictions along the members of such a covering family vanish.
2. **Detection on the affine ind-etale basis.** If $T$ is affine, a sheaf $\mathcal H$ vanishes if and only if $\mathcal H(W)=0$ for every $W$ in the affine ind-etale basis [def-weil-pbc-ind-etale-basis]. Consequently $u$ is an isomorphism if and only if, for every integer $n$ and every such $W$, the map of sections of its cohomology sheaves $\mathcal H^n(u)(W):\mathcal H^n(F)(W)\to\mathcal H^n(G)(W)$ is an isomorphism. For general $T$ use these bases over an affine open cover. No assertion is made that ordinary evaluation of an arbitrary complex on these basis objects preserves quasi-isomorphisms.
3. **Complexes of etale origin.** Let $\nu_T:T_{\mathrm{proet}}\to T_{\mathrm{et}}$ be [def-weil-pbc-site-comparison-morphism], and let $v:F'\to G'$ be a morphism in $D^+(T_{\mathrm{et}},\Lambda)$. Then $\nu_T^*v$ is an isomorphism if and only if for every geometric point $\bar t$ and every $n\in\mathbf Z$ its map on geometric stalks of cohomology sheaves is an isomorphism. Pro-etale geometric stalks are those of [def-weil-proetale-geometric-stalk]. In particular they are jointly conservative on all morphisms between the bounded constructible objects $\Dbc(T_{\mathrm{proet}},\Lambda)$, defined as objects of etale origin in [def-weil-pbc-proetale-modules].
4. **Warning about geometric points.** In general, geometric-point stalks are not conservative on all abelian sheaves on $T_{\mathrm{proet}}$, although the covering-family and basis criteria above remain valid there. For $T=\operatorname{Spec}k$ with $k$ algebraically closed and a nonzero abelian group $A$, let $\mathcal Q_A$ be the sheafified quotient of the sheaf of all set maps $|U|\to A$ by the constant abelian sheaf. On affine objects it has values $\mathcal Q_A(U)=\operatorname{Map}(|U|,A)/\operatorname{LC}(|U|,A)$, where locally constant means constant on an open neighbourhood of each point. Then $\mathcal Q_A(T)=0$ and all its geometric-point stalks are zero, but $\mathcal Q_A\ne0$.

proof.text: For a covering $\{U_i\to T\}$ and any object $V\to T$, the family $\{V\times_TU_i\to V\}$ is covering. The slice-site identification and restriction formula identify $\mathcal H|_{U_i}(V\times_TU_i\to U_i)$ with $\mathcal H(V\times_TU_i)$. If each restriction is zero, these groups vanish, and the sheaf equalizer axiom makes $\mathcal H(V)$ a subgroup of their zero product. Thus $\mathcal H=0$. Conversely restriction of the zero sheaf is zero. This is valid also for an empty covering of the empty scheme.

proof.text: Restriction to $U_i$ is exact by the cited restriction theorem. For modules over a possibly noncommutative constant ring, apply its underlying abelian restriction: kernels inherit the scalar action and cokernels carry the induced action, so their underlying abelian sheaves are the abelian kernels and cokernels. Hence restriction preserves $\mathcal H^n=\ker d^n/\operatorname{im}d^{n-1}$. Apply the unbounded derived isomorphism criterion to $u$ and to each restricted $u$. Each $\mathcal H^n(u)$ is invertible precisely when its kernel and cokernel vanish; exact restriction preserves these two sheaves, and step 1 detects their vanishing. This proves clause (1). A complex is acyclic precisely when all its cohomology sheaves vanish, by the quasi-isomorphism definition.

source.place: Tag 0991, section-points; blueprint Proof Step 1, corrected derived-category interpretation

proof.text: For affine $T$, the cited basis theorem says restriction determines sheaves and detects their isomorphisms. Apply it to $0\to\mathcal H$ to obtain the asserted zero-sheaf criterion. A natural transformation between sheaves on the basis is invertible if and only if its component maps are invertible: the component inverses are natural by composing the original naturality equations with them. Apply this to each $\mathcal H^n(u)$, then the unbounded derived isomorphism criterion. For a general $T$, first restrict to every member of an affine open cover and apply clause (1), then apply the affine test on each member. This uses sections of cohomology sheaves, not cohomology of ordinary section complexes.

source.place: Proof Step 2, replacing the false ordinary-evaluation inference

proof.text:
The comparison morphism has finite-limit-preserving inverse image on sets and the specified adjunction on fixed-$\Lambda$ module sheaves. Lift the finite limits sectionwise to abelian groups and scalar actions; they are limits of the underlying sheaves. Its left adjoint preserves finite colimits by the cited adjoint-colimit theorem. Thus $
u_T^*$ is exact on left module sheaves for finite rings, without a commutativity assumption. Preservation of kernels and cokernels gives naturally $\mathcal H^n(
u_T^*K)\cong
u_T^*\mathcal H^n(K)$. The new comparison-stalk lemma then identifies the stalk map of $\mathcal H^n(
u_T^*v)$ with that of $\mathcal H^n(v)$. Exactness of the pro-etale stalk functor is given by the classical-stalk lemma, so this is also the derived stalk criterion, independent of representatives. The canonical comparisons commute with $v$ by the naturality stated in the comparison-stalk lemma. No cofinality of etale neighbourhoods inside weakly etale neighbourhoods is assumed.

source.place: Tag 0GLZ, lemma-describe-pullback-from-etale; Tag 0993, lemma-classical-point; corrected blueprint Proof Step 3

proof.text:
If all stalk maps of $
u_T^*v$ are invertible, step 4 says every geometric stalk of every $\mathcal H^n(v)$ is invertible. The etale sheaf conservativity theorem, applied to underlying abelian sheaves, makes $\mathcal H^n(v)$ invertible; its inverse is automatically $\Lambda$-linear by the naturality of scalar actions. The unbounded derived criterion then makes $v$ invertible, and its inverse is sent to an inverse of $
u_T^*v$. The reverse implication follows by applying the exact stalk functors to an isomorphism. For arbitrary morphisms $a:K	o L$ in $\Dbc$, choose isomorphisms $K\cong
u_T^*K'$ and $L\cong
u_T^*L'$ from its definition. Fullness of the bounded-below comparison functor supplies a morphism $v:K'	o L'$ whose image is the conjugate of $a$. The preceding argument applies to $v$; conjugating by the chosen isomorphisms proves the assertion for $a$. Here full faithfulness is needed for lifting arbitrary morphisms of the essential image, not just objects.

source.place: Tag 0991, section-points; blueprint Proof Step 3, including arbitrary morphisms between constructible objects

proof.text: For $T=\operatorname{Spec}k$ with $k$ algebraically closed, define $\mathcal Q_A$ by the functions-quotient lemma. Its affine formula applies because the only point of $T$ is closed with separably closed residue field. At $U=T$ every function is constant, so $\mathcal Q_A(T)=0$. The strict localization at any geometric point of $T$ is $T$ itself: for every affine pointed etale neighbourhood, the cited lift-factorization theorem factors the geometric lift through $\operatorname{Spec}k$. The factorization is unique because affine scheme maps are ring maps and the fixed embedding $k\to\Omega$ is injective. Thus the identity pointed neighbourhood is initial in the affine pointed neighbourhood category. Its ring is terminal in the opposite ring diagram, so the colimit ring in the strict-localization definition is $k$. The classical-stalk lemma gives $\mathcal Q_{A,\bar t}=\mathcal Q_A(T)=0$ for every geometric point, including extensions of $k$.

Take $E=\mathbf N\cup\{\infty\}$, with each integer isolated and neighbourhoods of $\infty$ containing all but finitely many integers. This space is compact: an open-cover member containing $\infty$ leaves only finitely many integers to cover. Two distinct integers are separated by their singleton opens; an integer $r$ and $\infty$ are separated by $\{r\}$ and $E\setminus\{r\}$, so the space is Hausdorff. Each integer singleton is closed as well as open, and each cofinite tail containing $\infty$ is open with a finite open complement. These singletons and tails form a clopen basis and separate every two points, so every connected subset has at most one point. Let $E_n=\{0,\ldots,n-1,\infty\}$, and truncate later integers to $\infty$. The truncation maps identify $E$ with $\varprojlim E_n$: a compatible tuple either stays $\infty$ forever or eventually selects one fixed integer; the inverse-limit cylinder topology is precisely the topology just described. Put $B=\varinjlim\operatorname{Map}(E_n,k)$. Every stage is a finite product of copies of $k$, hence this is an ind-Zariski, in particular ind-etale, $k$-algebra. Ind-etale stability makes $U=\operatorname{Spec}B\to T$ weakly etale, so $U$ is an affine pro-etale object. Identify $B$ with $\operatorname{LC}(E,k)$: every locally constant function factors through a finite stage by the cited factorization theorem; two stage functions become equal on a common longer stage whenever their pullbacks to $E$ agree, because projections $E\to E_n$ are surjective. The cited prime-spectrum theorem identifies $|U|$ with $E\times\operatorname{Spec}k=E$. Choose $a\in A$, $a\ne0$, and the function equal to $a$ at $\infty$ and zero at every integer. Every neighbourhood of $\infty$ contains integers, so the function is not locally constant. Its class is nonzero in the quotient formula from step 6. Thus $\mathcal Q_A(U)\ne0$, proving clause (4): $0\to\mathcal Q_A$ is a non-isomorphism with isomorphic geometric stalks.
